title: SQLite delivery and readback: clear, write, read back in one project
proves: a project declares one SQLite client in the entry and uses it in three steps: clear the table, write the orders, read them back
a normal run writes 12 rows to the SQLite table and the readback product returns 12 rows; a second run clears first and gives the same rows

the run checks values: an <assert> on every readback row (status set) and an <assert> on a totals row (row count, id sum, amount sum, status count) of the rows that the seed writes; a wrong or stale table fails the run

Build needs an environment binding for the client and reads the table in the project (db/s39_shop.sqlite, the 12 rows that the seed writes): it proves the readback product against the table as it is on disk
Build does not prove that the load wrote the rows: Build isolates the write target and skips the clear, so the readback in Build shows the fixture rows, not the generated rows

a readback needs a literal count: without count Build cannot prove the cardinality and reports the capture as unknown, not DM211, because the lint of a step sees the client that the entry declares (#493); a count above the rows of the table stops the source early (DM316)

the table comes from a checked-in SQLite file, because Build refuses an <execute> step (unsupported_bounded_operation): a project that needs no readback of a checked-in table can create its own with createTable (s59_create_table)

a SQL script on a missing table, a selector on a missing table and a selector with invalid SQL all fail the run with the category sqlite_error, never with a guessed table_not_found, and without the SQL text; the message says to check the database name and to leave the .sqlite suffix out (#684)

patch.old: SELECT id, status, amount_cents FROM orders ORDER BY id
patch.new: SELEC id, status, amount_cents FROM orders ORDER BY id
